messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes and continuous batching assumptions

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick written recap and next steps so we can align internally and with your engineering team.

Key takeaways (from today's call):
- Current POC traffic: ~3M tokens/day (sporadic). Target ramp: 10M tokens/day within ~6 months; target long-term run-rate >=100M/month.
- Typical request size: ~700-900 tokens total (prompt + response).
- Traffic pattern: steady business-hours volume with ~3x peak bursts during launches; some background async inference overnight.
- Budget posture: target efficiency; willing to explore $/1M-token targets at scale. You mentioned aiming for ~$10/1M tokens as a reference.

Open items / asks:
1) Can you confirm a realistic monthly token target range (low / expected / high) for pricing (e.g., 10M / 100M / 300M)?
2) Do you have a firm target $/1M tokens at scale (please state threshold volumes associated with that target)?
3) Any hard latency or p99 SLOs we should assume for the model endpoints?
4) Are model variants fixed (e.g., one family) or will you switch between models (affects cache efficiency)?

Attached: token-volume-sheet.csv (template) — please fill the expected volumes and sample request size distribution, this will help our pricing & batching sims.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill volumes in the sheet (1-2 business days) -> we provide preliminary unit-econ estimates & batching assumptions.
- Technical workshop (30-60m) to align on continuous-batching expectations and concurrency.

Thanks — I'll follow up once I have the sheet populated from your side.

—Camila

Thanks Camila — appreciate the summary. Quick answers inline: 

Monthly token targets (low / expected / high):
- Low: 30M/month (current steady POC if we stay conservative)
- Expected: 100M/month (target within 4-6 months if POC converts)
- High: 300M+/month (aggressive growth scenario)

Average tokens per request: ~850 (we see ~300 tokens prompt, ~550 tokens generation on average).
Concurrency / traffic shape:
- Typical RPS: 6-8 steady during business hours
- Peak RPS: up to ~45-60 during launches/bursts (short windows)
- Many small interactive calls and a smaller % of long generation jobs (batchable).

Budget / target $/1M tokens:
- For planning, we're aiming for ~$10/1M tokens at scale (>=100M/month). If you can show unit economics at $8–$12/1M with batching assumptions, that will help the CFO.

Latency: p95 ~500ms target for short interactive flows; p99 can be higher for long generations (we're tolerant up to 5s).

Next steps: I'll complete token-volume-sheet.csv by end of day tomorrow. Happy to schedule the technical workshop after you and your infra team review the sheet.

—Samir

Samir — perfect, thanks for the detail. That gives us enough to run a first-pass cost model. A few quick notes from our side and a preliminary unit-econ example: 

Preliminary unit economics (ballpark, subject to model & quantization):
- Example baseline (no batching / on-demand): $18–$25 per 1M tokens for the model class you described.
- With continuous batching + prefix/KV cache and quantized execution (typical for steady workloads), we expect 2–3x improvement in effective throughput -> indicative price at scale: $7–$12 per 1M tokens.
- Given your target of ~$10/1M at >=100M/month, we can model a $9/1M offering as a starting point for discussion (requires ~consistent steady arrivals and willingness to accept batching-friendly behavior for some requests).

Assumptions tied to the $9/1M example: 
- Average request size: 850 tokens
- Effective batching ratio: ~2.5x (i.e., continuous batching + KV cache reduces GPU work roughly 2.5x vs naive runs)
- Target latency SLO for interactive flows: p95 <= 500ms — we'll preserve that by routing interactive traffic to lower-batch lanes while batching background/async requests.

Questions / clarifications we need to finalize pricing:
1) Percent of traffic that is latency-sensitive interactive vs batchable async (rough % split).
2) Model family / size you expect to run most frequently (we need this to pick kernel & quantization profile).
3) Any contractual requirements (SLA, retention, compliance) that should be factored into Dedicated/Private pricing?

Attaching a draft SOW skeleton that outlines volume breakpoints and proposed pricing tiers — please review and we'll update per your sheets.

If the numbers look directionally good, can we schedule the technical workshop next Wed (4/1) or Thu (4/2)? I'll loop in Aditya from our infra team to cover batching/concurrency assumptions.

Thanks,
—Camila

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes and continuous batching assumptions

Looping in a short technical note on continuous batching & concurrency assumptions so we're all aligned prior to the workshop.

Key assumptions for the $9/1M continuous-batching example:
- Continuous arrival model: sustained stream of small-to-medium requests (tens to hundreds of requests/sec) where the runtime can maintain an open batching window and KV cache. This yields the 2–3x effective throughput improvement mentioned.
- Batching window: for interactive lanes we keep windows small (~10–30ms) to avoid adding visible latency; for background/async lanes windows are larger (~50–200ms) to maximize packing.
- Concurrency: assume steady concurrency of O(10s) per GPU for interactive lane, O(100s) for batched lanes depending on model size. Burst capacity should be provisioned (or auto-burst to Dedicated) to handle the 45–60 RPS launch spikes you mentioned.
- Cache effectiveness: prefix/KV cache helps a lot if you have repeated prefixes or short-turn context reuse; if your workload is highly unique per-request, expect lower gains.

Suggested technical next steps (proposed workshop agenda):
1) Validate request-size distribution & percent batchable from your filled sheet.
2) Map model family -> quantization profile -> expected tokens/sec per GPU (we'll run a quick perf sim).
3) Run a 48-hour continuous-batching sim (staging) using your arrival pattern to measure real throughput, latency mix, and cost.
4) Review results and finalize volume pricing tiers + SLA lane definitions.

Proposed dates: Wed 2026-04-01 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2026-04-02 14:00–15:00 PT — please confirm.

I'll attach a short assumptions doc that outlines the perf model and the sim steps. Happy to discuss on the call.

—Aditya
